summary: Claim header normalization causes conditional RBAC role expressions to evaluate false in private deployment
description: Customers on the private deployment report sudden 403s for administrative API calls that rely on conditional RBAC rules evaluated against JWT custom claims. Errors started after an ingress edge upgrade in us-east. This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation for Arcana Health (private tenant).
impact: Multiple service accounts in the customer's private VPC receiving 403 on admin GraphQL routes; blocks operation automation and scheduled model rollouts. Estimated ~20% of ARC tenants impacted in us-east cluster during outage window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use service account token with custom claim 'tenant.env' set to 'arcana:prod' 2) Send POST to /admin/graphql route through customer's private ingress 3) Observe 403 with 'rbac:condition-eval-false' in response headers
observed_behavior: Requests that previously passed RBAC now fail with 403. Request logs show the claim header present but conditional expression in RBAC evaluated to false.
expected_behavior: Conditional expressions that reference JWT claim keys should evaluate using the original claim key names/values provided by the IdP exchange and preserved through the ingress path.
logs:
- proxy-access: 2026-03-10T08:12:14Z POST /admin/graphql 403 x-request-id=abc123
- auth-service: 2026-03-10T08:12:14Z claim 'tenant.env' found in token payload
- rbac-engine: 2026-03-10T08:12:14Z condition 'claims.tenant.env == "arcana:prod"' evaluated to false (input claims: tenant.Env="arcana:prod")
investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-10: Support reproduced issue with customer's token; confirmed mismatch in claim key casing during header propagation.
- Observed that the upgraded ingress (edge-proxy v3.7.0) started normalizing header names by capitalizing dotted claim keys (e.g., tenant.env -> tenant.Env) when serializing into X-JWT-CLAIMS header.
- RBAC engine uses case-sensitive JSON path lookups for condition evaluation; mismatch causes expression to short-circuit.
- Cross-checked with ingress change log and found PR that touched header canonicalization logic (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1569).
- Quick test: modifying RBAC condition to use a case-insensitive extractor returns correct allow; however this is not feasible for all customers.
- Correlated timeline with customer report and internal deploys; regression introduced during 2026-03-09 midnight deployment to us-east nodes.

root_cause: Ingress edge-proxy v3.7.0 introduced header canonicalization that changed the casing of dotted claim keys when serializing JWT claims into the X-JWT-CLAIMS header. The RBAC engine evaluates JSONPath expressions in a case-sensitive manner, so tenant-specific conditional policies referencing 'tenant.env' failed when header became 'tenant.Env'.
short_term_workaround:
1) Roll back edge-proxy to v3.6.8 for affected us-east nodes (completed in canary, scheduled cluster rollback).
2) Customer can temporarily rewrite RBAC conditions to use a case-insensitive claim accessor or normalize claim keys in policies.
resolution: Performed staged rollback of edge-proxy to v3.6.8 in us-east cluster (rolled out 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC). Deployed edge-proxy patch v3.7.1 with preserved claim key casing and unit tests on 2026-03-12 10:30 UTC. Verified Arcana's admin calls succeed post-deploy.
verification_steps: 1) Confirmed admin GraphQL POSTs from Arcana succeed with previously failing service-account tokens. 2) RBAC engine logs show condition evaluation true for claims. 3) Customer executed CI job that previously failed — now green.
